module8: Capstone: a full brand and document project
Real work joins design, documents and rules in one job. In this capstone you plan, build, check and hand over a small brand pack and a signed document, then show others how to reuse it.
Plan first: audience, one message, list of pieces, deadline and who approves.
Build the set: a brand kit, two templates, a fillable form and a final export for print and web.
Run the check list before handover: facts, spelling, contrast, rights and accessibility.
Hand over with a short guide so another person can reuse the templates without help.
A small shop needs a poster, a social post and a booking form. One kit gives all three the same colours and fonts, and the form is signed and filed with an audit record on the first day.
Produce a brand kit, two templates, one fillable form and one export set for a practice business, then let a peer make a new piece from your guide.
All items pass the check list; the peer makes a correct piece in 15 minutes; files are named with date and version.
quiz: A logo must print on a business card and on a large banner. Should it be a photo file or a vector file, and why?
A vector file, because it stays sharp at any size. A photo is made of pixels and blurs when enlarged.
A campaign needs 24 pieces in 3 languages. How do you keep quality high and fast?
Batch the repeat edits, make a version for each language and market, and run one check list before publishing covering facts, spelling, rights and accessibility.
A flyer has three fonts, five colours and four messages. What would you change?
Cut it to two fonts, the brand colours and one message with one clear action. Then check that the contrast is readable.
At the capstone handover another person must reuse your templates. What two things do you give them and how do you test it?
Give a project folder with a brand kit and templates plus a short guide. Test it by letting a peer make a correct new piece in about 15 minutes without help.
A 12 MB photo must go on a web page. What do you do?
Edit a copy and export a web size, for example about 300 KB, keeping the original untouched. Check it still looks clean.
What does a non-destructive edit mean, and why use layers?
The original pixels are never changed, so you can undo or adjust later. Layers hold each edit separately.
Name three steps to make a PDF agreement accessible.
Add proper headings, add alt text to pictures and set a correct reading order. Then run the accessibility check.
A form is signed electronically by two people. What record should you keep and why?
Keep the audit trail showing who signed and when. It is the evidence that the signature is genuine.
Ten staff make posters from one template. What should be locked and what should be open?
Lock logo, colours and fonts; leave text and picture open. This keeps the brand safe while allowing quick work.
A picture licence ended last month. How does a rights register help?
It records the licence end date, so the picture is removed before it is used again. It also shows who owns the check.
ladder: L1 Basic
Remember the difference between photo files and vector files, and name the tool for each job. Save a source file and an export with a clear name.
Show a zoomed photo and a zoomed logo side by side. Common mistake: using a small photo logo on a large banner.
L2 Awareness
Understand how grid, spacing, two fonts and strong contrast make one message clear. Explain why less is often better.
Ask learners to find the one message in a flyer. Common mistake: adding extra pictures and colours.
L3 Foundation
Apply layers, crop and light correction to edit photos without harming the original. Export the right size for print, web and social.
Check file sizes and that originals are untouched. Common mistake: saving over the only copy.
L4 Practitioner
Apply PDF tools to combine, protect and fill documents and request a signature. Make the file accessible with headings and alt text.
Run the accessibility check together. Common mistake: scanning a page as a picture so the text cannot be read by screen readers.
L5 Specialist
Analyse how a shared kit and locked templates keep a brand consistent. Compare a template that works with one that people break.
Test the template with a peer who has not seen it. Common mistake: leaving too many parts open to change.
L6 Advanced
Evaluate a batch of campaign pieces against a check list and a results sheet. Decide which version worked better and why.
Ask for facts, rights and access to be checked for every piece. Common mistake: judging results on taste, not numbers.
L7 Super expert
Create a full project and an operations pack with seats, rights register, archive rules and onboarding. Teach others to reuse it.
Check that every rule has an owner and a date. Common mistake: no yearly review, so unused seats and expired rights go unnoticed.
